project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 321 (System rejects live order submission without an explicit flag, defaulting to shadow mode against a sub-account)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 321 in the existing router member (packages/router, import name router; seat src/app/modules/router): a *live-submission gate*, `require_live_flag(mode, *, live_flag="live")` (and an `OrderMode` value type plus a `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised` error), that refuses to place a live order unless the order request carries an explicit opt-in flag, and that otherwise resolves the order to shadow mode against a sub-account. This is the safety gate the order path's other router features deliberately do not carry: feature 312's rounding and feature 313's minimum-notional check are properties of the order *values* (they validate the price and quantity against the venue grid the exchangeInfo store, feature 310, persists), while feature 321 is a property of the order's *authority* — whether the caller has explicitly elected to send real orders to the live venue at all. The two sentences have different repairs and different greppable codes, and the workspace's error-vocabulary discipline (no member imports another; a shared helper that raises another feature's error type defeats the caller's `except`) forbids feature 321 from borrowing feature 312/313's value-check errors. So feature 321 adds its own code, `live_not_authorised`, and its own error class, in the same member, as a sibling of the router member's existing `RouterError` vocabulary under that same base — not a new member, not a new component, not a new table. The footprint is three production files and their test: one new module (`packages/router/src/router/order_gate.py`) plus two small edits to existing files in that member (its error vocabulary and its `__init__.py` re-export). The gate is a *judgment over a mode the caller already has*, not a mode the feature decides: the order request that reaches the router already states whether it is a live order or a shadow order (feature 314's passive/aggresive choice, feature 316's client order id, all presuppose an order that has already been classified as live or shadow), so feature 321 takes the mode as an argument — the same verdict-gate shape feature 187's headline refusal, feature 230's admission gate and feature 275's pool floor take — and refuses when the mode is live and the explicit flag was not supplied. The default is shadow: a request that names no mode, or names a mode the gate cannot confirm as live, is resolved to shadow mode against the configured sub-account, never silently admitted as live. The explicit flag is a keyword of the gate, defaulting to the string "live", validated to be a non-empty string so a flag that is not an account selector cannot silently admit an order. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited; no new `@register` component is added (the router member's single `"router"` component, feature 310's exchangeInfo store, is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/<member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.router, app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/router/tests/`). Feature 321 is a pure judgment over a string the caller already has, so it adds no third-party dependency: it is a comparison over the order's mode and the explicit flag. Measure the real numbers by running the suite before relying on them. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, frozen dataclasses for value types, docstrings that cite app_spec.xml feature numbers and docs/alpha-engine-prd.md / docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md sections, stdlib-only computation, `@register` only in the package `__init__` (never a submodule — a submodule's registration fires only on the first `create_app()` of a process), degrade-don't-break composition (a builder that raises would take composition down for every unrelated feature, so a builder returns `None` for a deployment that names no store), member-owned tables created lazily beside the only module that writes them (never in the shared migration chain, which is order-sensitive and excluded from this feature's file claim), and the error-vocabulary discipline that no member imports another and a shared helper that raises another feature's error type defeats the caller's `except` (translate at the seam). The router member already lives in this workspace (packages/router: the exchangeInfo narrowing module, the append-only exchangeInfo version store, the error vocabulary holding RouterError / RouterFilterError / RouterStoreError, and the `__init__` that re-exports and fires `@register("router")`, seat src/app/modules/router). Feature 321 is a sibling within that member, not a new member. The governing documents are docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §M4 ("Paper trading against the live feed with real order placement on a sub-account. Pre-register success criteria in a hashed file before the shadow run starts") and §17 ("Separate keys per environment. The shadow sub-account key must not work on the live account"), and docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §16's live metrics and the M4 milestone ("live/book, live/exec in shadow mode, forward").

category.name: Order Routing & Venue Filters
category.feature: System rejects live order submission without an explicit flag, defaulting to shadow mode against a sub-account.

project_specification.integration_points: The gate is a pure judgment over an order's mode the caller already has, added to the router member (packages/router) as a sibling of feature 310's exchangeInfo store. It is reached directly from the member (`from router import require_live_flag, OrderMode, LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised, LIVE_SUBMISSION_NOT_AUTHORISED_CODE`), the way feature 310's `resolve_router_filters` and its errors are, and — for a composed application — through the existing seat (`app.modules.router`), which already hands back feature 310's single `router` component; feature 321 adds no second component and edits no seat. The mode the judgment reads is the order request's own declared mode (live or shadow), which the caller obtains from the same order object it asks to judge, and the judgment never decides the mode itself. The explicit flag (default "live") is a keyword of the gate so a deployment may name the opt-in differently; it is validated to be a non-empty string. The shadow sub-account the gate defaults to is the account a deployment has already configured for shadow trading (the sub-account whose key, per docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §17, must not work on the live account) — the gate names that account as the destination of a demoted order, it does not open a connection to it. The caller wires the gate into the order path at the single point where an order is about to be submitted: it calls the gate with the order's mode, and on the refusal it either surfaces the error (when the caller expected a live order) or routes the order to shadow against the sub-account (when the caller supplied no mode).
project_specification.constraints: - Feature 321 is a gate on an order's *authority*, and is deliberately NOT feature 312's rounding or feature 313's minimum-notional check: it must use its own code, `live_not_authorised`, and its own error class, `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised`, a sibling of the router member's existing `RouterError` vocabulary under that same base. It must NOT reuse `RouterFilterError`, `RouterStoreError`, or any of feature 310-313's value-check errors for the live-authority refusal, and feature 310-313's existing behaviour, messages, codes and tests must be untouched. - No member imports another. The mode the judgment reads is obtained from the order request the caller already holds, never from a sibling member's import; the gate performs no I/O and opens no venue connection. - No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited. No new `@register` component is added — feature 310's single `"router"` component is untouched, and feature 321 adds no component, no table, and no seat export. - The gate is a judgment over a mode, not a decision the feature makes: `require_live_flag(mode, *, live_flag="live")` takes the order's mode as an argument and returns the resolved mode (shadow when the mode is not confirmed live); it raises `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised` only when the mode is live and the explicit flag was not supplied. - The explicit flag defaults to "live" and is validated to be a non-empty string; the order's mode is validated to be a string. A mode that is not a recognised order mode (neither live nor shadow) is resolved to shadow, never admitted as live — failing safe. - The refusal message opens with the code `live_not_authorised`, states the supplied mode and the flag that was required, states the repair (supply the explicit live flag, or submit in shadow mode against the sub-account), and names the governing document (§M4 / §17). - The shadow default is the sub-account a deployment has configured for shadow trading (docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §17's separate shadow key); the gate names that account as the destination of a demoted order, it does not open a connection to it or hold its credentials. - All existing tests in the router member (packages/router/tests) and in tests/ must stay green. The member's own suite must be run explicitly (it is not graded by the bare `uv run pytest` gate). - Do not edit the order-sensitive shared files: src/app/middleware.py, src/app/settings.py, migrations/versions/**, alembic/versions/**.

implementation_steps.step: Phase 1 — the value type, the code and the class. The footprint is three production files and their test: one new module plus two small edits to existing files. (1) Add a `LIVE_SUBMISSION_NOT_AUTHORISED_CODE = "live_not_authorised"` constant and a `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised( RouterError)` error class to the member's existing error vocabulary as a sibling of feature 310's three classes. (2) Add an `OrderMode` value type — a frozen, string-valued type with the two members the order path recognises, `SHADOW` and `LIVE`, the shadow sub-account being the destination of a demoted order (docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §M4, §17) — and `require_live_flag(mode, *, live_flag="live")` to one new module, `packages/router/src/router/ order_gate.py`: a pure function that validates `mode` is a string and `live_flag` is a non-empty string, resolves an unrecognised or shadow mode to shadow (failing safe, never admitting as live), and raises `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised` (message opening with `live_not_authorised`, stating the supplied mode and the required flag, the repair, and §M4/§17) when the mode is live and the explicit flag was not supplied. (3) Re-export `OrderMode`, `require_live_flag`, `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised` and the code constant from the member's existing `__init__` alongside feature 310's existing names. No new component, table, or seat export.

Phase 2 — the tests. Add one test module, `packages/router/tests/test_order_gate.py`, asserting: an explicit live flag admits a live order (returns live); a live order without the flag is refused with `live_not_authorised` (the error opens with the code, names the supplied mode and the required flag, states the repair, and cites §M4/§17); a shadow order is admitted and resolves to shadow; an unrecognised or absent mode resolves to shadow rather than admitting as live (fail safe); the explicit flag is a parameter (a custom flag changes what counts as the opt-in) and is validated (an empty or non-string flag is refused in the gate's own vocabulary); the mode is validated (a non-string mode is refused); `LiveSubmissionNotAuthorised` is a `RouterError` and a sibling of feature 310's three classes (not a subclass of `RouterFilterError` or `RouterStoreError`); and feature 310-313's vocabulary is unchanged (the existing router tests asserting the member's exports and errors are preserved — feature 321 adds names, it does not remove or reword any).

Phase 3 — verify. Run the router member's own suite (`uv run pytest packages/router/tests`) and the repository-level suite (`uv run pytest tests/`) — both, since the member suite is not graded by the bare gate — and confirm all pass. Lint only the changed files against a sibling (the repo lint is red on main). Confirm feature 310-313's behaviour and tests are untouched, that no new component is registered (`scan_components` still reports exactly one `router` component), and that no order-sensitive shared file was edited.
